summary: Coos County fire tower site that the FFLA marks gone; NH Family Hikes lists a Mill Mountain (Stark) among mountains that once had a fire tower. No source found gives its build, staffing or removal dates.

events.note: Statewide, not specific to this site: NH Family Hikes says all remaining state fire towers were closed on June 9, 1983. The source does not name Mill Mountain.

evidence.supports: FFLA county list: Mill Mountain, Coos County, at 44.59626, -71.38622, tower gone
NH Family Hikes: Mill Mountain (Stark) at 2517 feet
NH Family Hikes: Mill Mountain is placed under the heading for mountains that once had a fire tower
evidence.quote: Mountains which Once Had a Fire Tower

evidence.supports: All remaining New Hampshire fire towers closed on June 9, 1983

notes_for_editor: Thin evidence: the only two sources are a county directory entry and a hiker's history list, so the story is shorter than the 120-word floor. Identity is assumed, not confirmed: NH Family Hikes gives Mill Mountain (Stark) at 2517 feet, and the FFLA gives Mill Mountain in Coos County with no town. Both list the site as no longer having a tower, so the status agrees across sources. An earlier version of this record said NH Family Hikes filed Mill Mountain under 'Other Standing Fire Towers'; that was wrong. Checked 2026-10-21 against the cached page, the entry sits under 'Mountains which Once Had a Fire Tower', so the earlier status conflict does not exist. The state's history PDF (nhdfl.dncr.nh.gov forest-lookout-towers-history.pdf) returns HTTP 403 to fetch_text, and a search snippet from it mentions Mill Mountain alongside West Royce in a squirrel-card passage; that passage was not read or quoted. A readable copy of that PDF, or a Coos County historical society record, would be the best next source. The record's agency, access and visit fields stay unknown: no source describes ownership or access.
